text:
mia: pushing the memory-tiering KV cache sweep results. TL;DR: paging-heavy workloads show big p95 regressions in eu-west for H100 when hit rate drops below ~72% :chart_with_upwards_trend:
bench-bot: automated run complete: 1719456800. jobs: kv-tiering-sweep-v2. results uploaded to internal://bench/kv-tiering/1719456789/ (csv + plots)
arjun: saw the csv — interesting. can you paste the p50/p95 for seq=4096 vs seq=512 across regions?
mia: quick paste from the summary table:
```
A100-us-west1  seq512 p50=18ms p95=46ms hit=89%
A100-us-west1  seq4096 p50=45ms p95=220ms hit=62%
H100-eu-west1   seq512 p50=14ms p95=38ms hit=86%
H100-eu-west1   seq4096 p50=60ms p95=480ms hit=68% <-- huge tail
H100-ap-southeast1 seq4096 p95=260ms hit=75%
```
jen: wow that eu-west p95 for long sequences is rough. do we have eviction policy logged per run? LRU vs seg-LRU?
sam: runs were: default LRU, gen2 (two-tier), and aggressive prefetch on/off. I can paste the p95 deltas from gen2 vs LRU: gen2 improved p95 for seq4096 by ~1.6x in us-west but only ~1.2x in eu-west.
lia: hypothesis: kernel selection + PCI topology in eu-west region is causing slower page-in for large KV segments. also H100's kernel tiling for kv lookup might be suboptimal for very long continuations.
arjun: can we confirm if kernel fallback occurred? i.e., fused attention path vs fallback to generic kernel which hurts throughput?
mia: bench-bot logs show a kernel fallback flag for the worst runs in eu-west at around seq >= 2048. bench-bot: note: fallback_count=87 for run id 1719456789-eu-h100
jen: do we have any bandwidth metrics? nvlink vs pcie transfers per batch?
sam: yes — sample from perf-export: avg kv-page transfers per request for seq4096: us-west(A100)=0.9MB req, eu-west(H100)=2.7MB req (explains higher latency).
lia: eviction policy suggestion: try size-aware segmented LRU where hot prefixes stay in GPU slab and large, cold entries are paged to host. should increase hit-rate for long prefixes.
mia: agree. action: run a 3x sweep toggling: (1) seg-LRU size-aware, (2) increase GPU slab from 1.5GB->3GB, (3) kernel-priority forcing fused path where possible. keep prefetch off for first pass.
jen: commands we used for baseline (for reproducibility):
```
./bench_ctl --model redwood-11b --gpu H100 --region eu-west1 \
  --seq-lens 64,512,2048,4096 --evict-policy lru --kv-slab 1.5GB --prefetch off \
  --emit csv --out /tmp/bench_eu.csv
```
arjun: also suggest logging per-token tail (p99.9) and adding a small jitter to request start times to avoid synchronous page storms.
sam: note: quantized runs (int8) had slightly better hit rate due to smaller item footprint; p95 improved by ~8% when we recomputed the cache footprint after quantization. worth noting for cost/latency tradeoffs.
bench-bot: scheduled follow-up sweep (id 1719460001) with seg-lru + larger slab + forced-kernel-priority. queued on eu-west1 H100 cluster. ETA ~4h.
mia: cool. if follow-up confirms, we should add a per-region default config: eu-west1: enable seg-lru, slab=3GB, kernel-priority=try-fused. us-west keep current defaults.
lia: aside: we should instrument prefix-length heatmaps to detect which prefix lengths drive the most page-ins; that'll guide smarter eviction.
jen: plotting suggestion: x=sequence length buckets, y=cache hit %, color=region, with p95 overlay line. that'll make tradeoffs clear in one chart.
arjun: agreed. also include kernel-fallback rate as an annotation.
mia: assigning tasks: @sam run the seg-lru + slab sweep (bench id 1719460001) and drop CSV to internal://bench/kv-tiering/1719456789/followup.csv. @lia add prefix heatmap hook to the runtime (small PR). @jen produce the combined chart once follow-up finishes.
sam: on it. starting run now. :rocket:
bench-bot: follow-up run started: 1719460001. status=running. logs streaming -> internal://bench/kv-tiering/1719456789/logs/1719460001
mia: thanks team. if the seg-lru tops out, next step is adaptive prefetch for seq>=1024 only. low-risk toggle. :thinking_face:
arjun: I'll watch p99.9; if that drops without hurting p50 we can rollout a canary. :eyes:
jen: ping when follow-up CSV is ready and i'll stitch the chart.
bench-bot: follow-up run finished: 1719460200. results: internal://bench/kv-tiering/1719456789/followup.csv, plots: internal://bench/kv-tiering/1719456789/followup_plots.zip
mia: quick summary after follow-up: seg-LRU + 3GB slab reduced eu-west seq4096 p95 from 480ms -> 260ms and hit rate improved 68% -> 81%. kernel-priority reduced fallback_count from 87->12. this is promising.
lia: nice. let's open a rollout PR for eu-west defaults and include an opt-out flag for customers who want raw LRU.
jen: will draft dashboard widget showing per-region KV hit rate and p95 trend.
arjun: can someone add a short note to the onboarding guide about region-specific defaults/expectations? I keep getting questions from infra team.
mia: will do. closing the thread after dashboards/doc PRs are up. :white_check_mark:
